paragraphs.source_en: I made my way around to the kitchen. The kitchen door stood open a crack, rattling incessantly in the autumn wind. The wind blowing in through the gap must at some point have put out the kerosene lamp; it was perhaps a moonlit night, for long shadows of moonlight reached in from the window. On the tray stood three glass tumblers, and in two of them there still remained half a glass of tea-colored liquid. Even hot water poured into glass somehow feels cold; how much more so this liquid, set quietly beside the fire-extinguishing jar under the chilly autumn moonlight, which seemed icy before it even touched the lips and gave one little desire to drink it. But then, one only learns the nature of things afterward. Take Tatara Sanpei: after drinking this stuff, his face turned scarlet and he breathed out hot, heavy breaths. Even I, a cat, might not be unable to grow merry for a while if I drank it. Life is bound to end sooner or later, so whatever there is to do should be done while life remains. It would be too late to die and then lament from the grave, “Ah, what a pity.” I urged myself on: “Take courage and drink.” So I thrust my tongue vigorously into the glass and lapped at it, pichapicha, several times. Good heavens, what a shock; the tip of my tongue tingled sharply, as though pricked by a needle. I cannot imagine what mad fancy drives humans to drink such foul-smelling stuff, but we cats cannot possibly drink it. Cats and beer simply do not get along. The first time I tasted it, I found it unbearable and drew back the tongue I had stuck out. Yet I reconsidered: “Humans are always saying that good medicine tastes bitter, and when they catch cold they drink strange things with grimacing faces. I have long wondered whether the medicine cures the illness, or whether they keep taking medicine after the illness has already cured itself. Now is the perfect chance to seek an answer to that question by means of beer. If drinking it merely leaves some bitterness in my belly, so be it; but if I become as pleasantly transported as Sanpei, I shall be a cat who has made an unprecedented bargain, and I may even teach the neighborhood cats about it. Well then, who knows what will happen? I entrust myself to heaven and resolve that I shall drink it down.” Thus I put my tongue into the glass once more. Knowing it would be hard to drink with my eyes open, I squeezed them shut tight and drank the beer again.

paragraphs.source_zh: 我转到了厨房。厨房的门开着一道缝儿，在秋风里哗啦哗啦地响个不停。从门缝里吹进来的风，不知什么时候将煤油灯吹灭了，可能是月夜吧，窗子外射进长长的月影。茶盘上放着三只玻璃杯子，其中有两只杯子还留有半杯茶色的液体。玻璃杯中即使注入开水，也会给人以一种冰凉的感觉，更何况是在凉意十足的秋夜，在月光的照射下，静静地放在消火缸旁边的这种液体，还没等沾唇就已经感到冷冰冰的，使人不太想喝了。但是，一切事物都是在事后才知道的嘛。像多多良三平，他喝了这种东西变得满脸通红，喘着热乎乎的气。即使我这只猫儿，只要喝了也不见得就不能高兴一阵子吧。反正这条命迟早是要结束的，无论什么事都要趁着这条命在干它一下。如果死后再在坟墓中悔恨地说什么“哎呀，太遗憾啦”之类的话，就来不及了。我鼓励自己说：“下决心喝吧。”于是我用劲把舌头伸进杯子里去，叭叽叭叽舔了几口。好家伙，真吓死我啦，舌尖就好像被针尖扎了一般，刺痛得很。人类不知从哪里来的这股疯劲，要喝这种臭烘烘的饮料，我们猫儿是喝不了这种东西的。猫儿和啤酒，怎么也是合不来的。我头一次尝时，感到受不了，把伸出的舌头缩了回来。不过，我又想：“人类经常说什么良药苦口，在感冒的时候，总是皱着眉头喝一些很怪的东西。我一直怀有疑问：到底是吃药吃好了病呢，还是病好了还在吃药呢？但是现在是最好的机会，把我这个疑问用啤酒来寻求个答案吧。如果喝下去，只是在肚子里感到一些苦味，那也就算啦，如果也能像三平君那样感到腾云驾雾似的愉快起来，那我就成了空前讨到便宜的猫儿，满可以教一教附近的那些猫儿啦。哎，天晓得将会怎样？我是听天由命了，下决心一定要把它喝下去。”就这样，我又把舌头伸进杯子里。我知道睁着眼睛是难以喝下去的，于是我紧紧闭上眼睛，又喝了一回啤酒。

paragraphs.source_en: When, by enduring and enduring, I at last finished off that half glass of beer, a curious phenomenon occurred. At first my tongue burned and tingled, and my mouth felt painfully as though being pressed from the outside. But after several laps it gradually became easier, and by the time I had emptied the first glass, it no longer required any special effort. I thought a little more would do no harm, and so disposed of the second glass as well. Finally I licked clean even the dregs spilled on the tray, sending every last drop into my stomach.

units.source_zh: 当我强忍着终于把这半杯啤酒喝光之后，一个奇妙的现象发生了。

units.source_en: At first my tongue burned and tingled, and my mouth felt painfully as though being pressed from the outside.

units.source_en: But after several laps it gradually became easier, and by the time I had emptied the first glass, it no longer required any special effort.
units.source_zh: 但是喝了几口之后就逐渐舒服多了，当喝光了第一杯的时候，也就用不着怎么特别费劲了。

units.source_zh: 我心想，再喝些也不要紧，于是又把第二杯给报销啦。

units.source_en: Finally I licked clean even the dregs spilled on the tray, sending every last drop into my stomach.
units.source_zh: 最后把洒在盘上的余汁也舔得干干净净，让它全都落进我的肚里。

paragraphs.source_zh: 当我强忍着终于把这半杯啤酒喝光之后，一个奇妙的现象发生了。最初是舌头感到火烧火燎一般，嘴里好像受外部压迫似的难受得很。但是喝了几口之后就逐渐舒服多了，当喝光了第一杯的时候，也就用不着怎么特别费劲了。我心想，再喝些也不要紧，于是又把第二杯给报销啦。最后把洒在盘上的余汁也舔得干干净净，让它全都落进我的肚里。

paragraphs.source_en: After that, for a while, I crouched there motionless in order to observe the condition of my body after drinking. My body grew warmer and warmer, my eyelids began to droop half open and half shut, and my ears flushed with heat. I wanted to sing; I wanted to dance the cat’s little jig. I felt as though Master, Meitei, Dokusen, all of them, could go to the devil. As for that old Kaneda, I wanted to rake him hard with my claws. And as for Kaneda’s wife, I wanted to bite a chunk out of her great nose. There were all sorts of things I wanted to do. At last I rose unsteadily to my feet, then staggered forward a few steps. I thought, “Now this is amusing. I must go outside for a walk. I shall go outside and bid the moon good evening. It is exceedingly pleasant.”

paragraphs.source_zh: 然后，我有一阵子为了解自己饮酒后的身体情况，一动不动地蹲在那里。身子越来越暖和，两眼的眼睑开始半睁半闭，耳朵也发起烧来。我要唱歌，想要跳猫儿蹦蹦舞。我有种感觉：什么主人、迷亭、独仙，都给我滚开！对于金田那老东西，我真想狠狠挠他一爪子。对金田的老婆，我也真想把她的大鼻子咬掉一块。我想干的事儿多着哪。最后，我晃晃悠悠地站立起来，又趔趔趄趄地走上几步。我心想：“这可有意思哟。我得到外边走走。我要走到外边去对月亮道声晚上好。真是痛快极啦。”

paragraphs.source_en: I suppose this is what people mean by being transported with delight. Aimlessly, in a state that was something like taking a stroll and something not quite like it, I moved my four unsteady legs along as best they would go. For some reason I was terribly sleepy. I could not tell whether I was asleep or walking; I felt my eyes were open, yet my eyelids seemed unbearably heavy. If things had come to this, then so be it. Whether before me lay a sea or a mountain, I would not be afraid of anything. Just as I limply put one foreleg forward, there came at once a splash; I had barely cried “Ah!” before I thought, now I am done for. Before I had time to think how I had been done for, I realized that my mind had fallen into utter confusion.

paragraphs.source_zh: 我想所谓陶然，就是指我现在的情况吧。我漫无目的地，以一种似散步又非散步的样子，移动着脚下不稳的四条腿向前走去。不知为什么我困倦得很。我不知自己是睡着了呢还是在走路，我感到自己是睁着眼睛，但又觉得眼皮沉重得很。既然这样，我就豁出去啦。管它刀山火海，我什么也不怕！我软瘫瘫地刚好把前腿向前一伸，立刻就发出了“扑通”一声响，我刚叫了一声“哎呀”，心想这回可出娄子了。我来不及想出了什么娄子，就发觉脑子乱了套。
